messages:
rachael: Heads-up — we're planning a short maintenance window next Tuesday 03:00–03:30 UTC to apply a kernel and runtime patch to Dedicated GPU hosts. A few questions: do we pin model versions for customers during the window? and what should the statuspage copy be?

sam_prodeng: Pin by default for any customer explicitly using a model version in their config. For unpinned routes we fallback to the pinned stable variant. Rollback trigger = >5% 5m error spike or latency P95 > 2s for 10m after rollout. If triggered, auto-roll back to previous pinned variant.

amy_support: Thanks. For customer comms we should call out impact: brief degraded throughput, possible short request timeouts. No data loss. Include a link to KB. Also note Dedicated customers with reserved capacity will see capacity preserved but possible increased latency.

jack_sales: Can we add a one-line reassurance for enterprise customers: "If you have a strict SLA, we can schedule an isolated maintenance at your request."

sam_prodeng: Agree. Operational notes: we'll create a canary group (5% traffic across eu-west and us-west) then ramp to 50% over 10m. If canary OK, ramp remaining traffic. Pinning plan: during window, any API request with explicit model_version stays; for unversioned requests we serve the last stable tag. We'll add a header X-Redwood-Model-Pinned: true/false for debugging.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by @sam_prodeng: maintenance/dedicated/2026-03-24-0300 -> in 6d. Canary: false -> will run canary at start of window.

amy_support: Draft statuspage snippet below — please copy/edit.

statuspage-bot: Suggested public snippet ready.

rachael: (Draft statuspage copy)

```
Incident type: Maintenance
Scheduled start: Tue 2026-03-24 03:00 UTC
Expected end: Tue 2026-03-24 03:30 UTC
Affected services: Dedicated GPU inference (short degraded throughput, intermittent timeouts possible)
Impact: Some requests may see increased latency or brief errors. No data loss. Customers with pinned model versions will continue to serve their pinned model.
What we are doing: Applying kernel and runtime patch to improve stability and security. We'll canary small % of traffic and rollback automatically on regressions.
Contact: support@redwood.ai / status.redwood.ai
```

rachael: (Draft customer email snippet)

```
Hi <Customer>,
We're performing a brief maintenance on Tue 24 Mar 2026 03:00–03:30 UTC to apply a security and runtime fix to Dedicated GPU nodes. During this window you may see slightly higher latency or occasional request timeouts. If you have a pinned model version, your traffic will continue to serve that version.
If you need a guaranteed isolated window, reply and we'll coordinate.
Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

sam_prodeng: +1. Add internal rollback checklist link: https://intranet.redwood/ops/rollback-checklist (ops only). Also ensure everyone tags incidents channel if rollback fires.

jack_sales: I'll prep a targeted email for the top 10 reserved capacity customers — we should call out they can request a bespoke maintenance slot.

rachael: Action items: amy to publish statuspage + email snippet, jack to run targeted outreach list, sam to upload pinning/rollback config to the runbook and kick the deploy job, I'll monitor the thread and post post-mortem summary. Plan looks good. :white_check_mark:

statuspage-bot: Statuspage update queued for Tue 2026-03-24 02:50 UTC for publish.

amy_support: Publishing draft now — will tag this thread when live.

rachael: Thanks team, will set a 02:50 reminder and escalate if canary shows anomalies.
